deep.reconstruction:
This page is item 3 of a programmatic outline, written in 1983 in the run-up to and alongside Pursuing Stacks, of what a general 'homotopy theory' (théorie homotopique) should contain. The previous page set up the data: a category M of 'models' with a class W of weak equivalences, the localisation Hot = W^{-1}M, homotopy invariants pi_0(x,y) = Hom_H(x,y) and pi_1(x,y;f), and a diagram-indexed version H(I), H(J). The next page concludes that, except perhaps f) and g), everything should be derivable from the pair (M, W ⊂ Fl(M)), and that one should 'find the right axioms'. The items here, in modern language:
(a) Models: their importance and their indeterminacy. Objects of M are presentations of objects of Hot, determined only up to weak equivalence.
(b) Long exact sequences 'of the two types' attached to an arrow f. These are the Puppe cofibre and fibre sequences. They come from cylinders and cocylinders (cylinder objects, path objects) of an object, and from mapping cylinders and cocylinders of a map between models. This is Quillen's Homotopical Algebra, ch. I.
(c) Left and right resolutions of a model, i.e. cofibrant and fibrant replacements. Also the formalism of derived functors when two homotopy theories are present: Quillen adjunctions and total derived functors.
(d) Homotopy notions on models ('homotopy structure': homotopy relation, 'homotopisms'). Resolutions are defined only up to homotopy. The margin remarks that these are intermediate notions used in constructing the derived objects.
(e) Homotopies between maps, homotopies between homotopies, and so on. One should probably have, for two models X, Y, an explicit object Hom(X,Y) in Hot. It would be given by a suitable complex (simplicial or other type) of higher homotopies. On H there would then be an external Hom with values in Hot, or in a richer theory. He notes that Quillen has simplicial Homs. In modern terms this is the mapping space, i.e. the enrichment of every homotopy theory over spaces, as in Dwyer–Kan simplicial localisation (1980) and later infinity-categories.
(f) Truncation operations, either global on models or deduced on H. These are Postnikov or t-structure truncations.
(g) Invariants Pi_i or H_i with values in a category, often abelian, attached to the theory. These are homotopy or homology functors, akin to the heart of a t-structure.
The bottom-left margin seems to say that f) and g) are structures particular to certain theories. This matches the next page's caveat that f) and g) may not follow from (M, W). Taken as a whole, the page is a table of contents for an axiomatic theory of homotopy theories presented by localisers.
errors: No mathematical errors; it is an outline. The suggestion in e) that Hom(X,Y) in Hot exists for any (M,W) is correct, but needs a construction such as Dwyer–Kan hammock localisation; the page leaves it as 'sans doute'.

ideas.what: Long exact (Puppe) sequences of both types attached to a map, built from cylinders and cocylinders
ideas.modern_name: Cofibre/fibre sequences in a model category

ideas.what: Left/right resolutions and derived functors between two homotopy theories
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks; Les Dérivateurs (derived functors as Kan extensions)

ideas.what: Every homotopy theory should carry a Hom(X,Y) with values in Hot built from higher homotopies (Hot-enrichment)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (discussion of homotopy types as coefficients, integrators)

ideas.what: Truncations and Pi_i/H_i invariants valued in an (often abelian) category attached to the theory, as possibly extra structure
Programme: everything should be derivable from (M, W); find the right axioms
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy theory = localiser / relative category; derivators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dwyer–Kan; Barwick–Kan relative categories; Grothendieck/Heller derivators

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly separates truncation structures and abelian-valued Pi_i/H_i invariants (f, g) as possibly not determined by (M, W). This anticipates the modern view that t-structures are extra data on a stable infinity-category. It is a mild documentary point, not a new result.
missed.quote: f) Opérations de troncation, soit globales sur modèle, soit déduites sur H. g) Invariants Πi ou Hi, à valeurs dans une catégorie (souvent abélienne) associée à la théorie.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical documentation of Grothendieck's 1983 outline of the axiomatics of homotopy theories; no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A standard programmatic outline (Quillen-style model category features plus Hot-enrichment). The Hot-valued Hom echoes Dwyer–Kan, done independently, and the f/g caveat is a nice touch, but none of it is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: c) likely reads 'formalisme de foncteurs dérivés' rather than 'fonctorialisation de foncteurs dérivés'.
e) 'et dans H un Hom externe à valeurs dans Hot' (H script, not Hot) seems more likely from the image.
f) 'soit déduites sur H' (script H) rather than 'Hot'.
b) the parenthesis '(cf.[?] des deux types)' is uncertain; it could be '(c'est des deux types)' or '(il y en a des deux types)'.
Bottom-left margin probably says f) and g) are structures particular to certain theories, consistent with next page's 'Sauf peut-être les structures f) et g)'.
